clue.text: Nobody faces such a blow

parts.note: a chop to the back of the neck is delivered from behind, so the victim never sees it coming

explanation.surface: A remark that this kind of punch is never taken face on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nobody' reads like an insult (a nobody), but it simply means no one.
explanation.definitionFit: A short chop to the back of the neck, the way a rabbit was once killed, is struck from behind.

clue.text: Withdraw to a place of seclusion

definitions.meaning: to pull back, as an army does
a quiet hideaway for rest or prayer

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for pulling back and a noun for a secluded refuge.

clue.text: Union notice one may object to

definitions.text: Union notice one may object to

parts.words: Union notice one may object to
parts.note: a marriage is a union, and the church reads out an announcement beforehand inviting objections

explanation.surface: A trade union circular that members might complain about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union; here it is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Church announcements of an intended wedding are read so that anyone with a lawful objection can speak.

clue.text: Under control wearing tartan

definitions.meaning: dressed in a checked pattern, tartan being a check

explanation.definitionFit: Restrained things are held this way; read literally, someone in tartan is clothed in a check pattern.

clue.text: Soft, but will stand up in small picture

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: pic is a short form of picture
to last is to hold out or endure

explanation.surface: Something gentle that nonetheless holds its own in a little photo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand up' suggests vertical posture; here it means endure.
explanation.definitionFit: Malleable material that can be moulded is described as yielding and pliable.

clue.text: One from Oslo perhaps wearing no make-up

indicators.note: a make-up is a composition, so the letters are made up into a new order

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian person going about without cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' looks like cosmetics but signals rearranging WEARING NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital of Norway, so a resident is a native of that country; 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: Isn't it used for cool-headed diplomacy?

definitions.text: Isn't it used for cool-headed diplomacy?

parts.words: Isn't it used for cool-headed diplomacy?
parts.note: the irony is that a direct phone link between capitals named for heat is meant to keep tempers cool

explanation.surface: A question about the tools of calm international relations.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct emergency telephone link between heads of government is used to defuse crises calmly.

clue.text: With sex-appeal, unusual antic that's devilish

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for sex appeal

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters appear in an unaccustomed order

explanation.surface: An odd and alluring trick that seems wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the letters of the clue's own word; 'that's' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the Devil, fiendish and wicked.

clue.text: Correct an argument over dues

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or quarrel
rights are what one is owed

explanation.surface: Fixing a dispute about money owed.
explanation.definitionFit: To put in order or make proper again is to rectify things.

clue.text: Inflationary apparatus coming from another area to the right

indicators.note: another version of the words, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A pump arriving from a different region, placed on the right side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' turns AREA TO into AERATO; R is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that pumps air into something, as into a liquid or soil, so it inflates in a loose sense.

clue.text: An odd bargain might be picked up at it

definitions.text: An odd bargain might be picked up at it

parts.words: An odd bargain might be picked up at it
parts.note: odd here means a leftover piece of cloth, sold off cheaply at a shop event

explanation.surface: A strange bargain picked up at some event.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale of leftover ends of fabric rolls at reduced prices.

clue.text: Trousers that Robert exclusively wore initially on Sunday

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed after another
initially picks the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Robert wears only certain trousers on Sundays.
explanation.walkthrough: TREWS are close-fitting tartan trousers, Scottish in origin.
explanation.definitionFit: Close-fitting tartan legwear traditionally worn in Scotland.

clue.text: Old mister upset French, man's immoderate views

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman's title

explanation.surface: An elderly gentleman angered by a Frenchman's extreme opinions.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding radical opinions far beyond the political mainstream.

clue.text: Two-way ticket in Australia

parts.note: a return ticket takes you there and returns you, the two words naming the remote interior of the country

explanation.surface: A return fare bought Down Under.
explanation.definitionFit: The remote, sparsely settled interior of Australia; split, its halves describe a journey there and home.

clue.text: Toil badly on gold surface first using this steering device?

indicators.note: the gold and surface pieces come before the toil piece

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the top is the upper surface

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters are put in poor order

explanation.surface: Labouring clumsily on a gilded layer while relying on automatic guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' signals an anagram of the clue's first word, which goes at the end; 'first' puts the gold and surface pieces ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An automatic system keeping an aircraft or ship on course without a human at the controls.

clue.text: Fancy it being a fire-spouting monster

definitions.meaning: the Greek mythical beast that breathed flames

explanation.surface: A fancy that turns into a dragon-like creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an illusory dream and the flame-breathing lion-goat-serpent of Greek myth.

clue.text: Type of selling still has first-class backing

parts.note: inert means motionless

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters are turned around

parts.note: A1 is first-class, written AI

explanation.surface: A sales method that remains top-notch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inertia selling' is sending unrequested goods and charging if they are not returned.
explanation.definitionFit: The word qualifies a sales practice that relies on customers' failure to act.

clue.text: Omission is no lie surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters come in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A remark that leaving something out is truthful.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping a sound or syllable in speech, as in 'can't'.

clue.text: Tell Ray travelling watchfully

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to tell Ray to stay alert on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: In a wide-awake, vigilant manner.

clue.text: A relatively dark patch seen initially in blazer pocket

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the sun is something that blazes
to pot is to pocket a ball in snooker or billiards

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of seen

explanation.surface: A stain spotted on the pocket of a jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blazer' looks like a jacket but is the sun, and 'pocket' is the verb; 'initially' gives S, which 'in' places between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooler region on the solar surface that appears darker than its surroundings.

clue.text: Clipper making off with the fleece?

definitions.meaning: humorously, one who takes the wool from a sheep, as if stealing it

explanation.definitionFit: A person who clips sheep, and so jokingly a thief walking off with their wool.

clue.text: Penny a long time with the lad who's a young attendant

parts.note: an age is a very long time
boy means lad

explanation.surface: A lad who has been a servant for ages for a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy who attends a bride or serves in a hotel.

clue.text: Only one strand coming from the wig?

definitions.text: Only one strand coming from the wig?

parts.words: Only one strand coming from the wig?
parts.note: a single hair is literally a piece of hair, taken from a false head of hair

explanation.surface: A single thread falling out of a wig.
explanation.definitionFit: A wig or toupee; read literally, one fragment of hair.

clue.text: Mother going round Greek capital finds molten rock

indicators.note: the mother word encircles the other letter

parts.note: mama is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: capital means the first, upper letter of Greek

explanation.surface: Mum on a trip around Athens discovers lava.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot liquid material beneath the earth's crust, which becomes lava when erupted.

clue.text: Test the heartless invader with a choral composition

indicators.note: an invader enters territory, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for cars

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letter of the word the

explanation.surface: Testing an unfeeling invader with a sung piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle letter of 'the', leaving TE; 'invader' makes that enter the car-test word.
explanation.definitionFit: A short sacred piece for unaccompanied voices.

clue.text: Pan runner William took back

parts.note: a ski is a runner on snow

indicators.note: back means the letters are read from end to start

parts.note: William Tell is the Swiss archer of legend

explanation.surface: A runner made off with William's saucepan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' could be the verb to criticise; here it is a frying pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A frying pan, especially a cast-iron one.

clue.text: Sort of value scoundrel put on island on the way back

indicators.note: in an across clue the first piece precedes the island piece

parts.note: a rat is a traitor or scoundrel

indicators.note: going in reverse, so the letters are read from right to left

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: A villain placed on an island as he travels home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rateable value' was the British assessed value of property for local tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a property's assessed worth for local taxation.

clue.text: Basic details to get down to

definitions.text: Basic details to get down to

parts.words: Basic details to get down to
parts.note: the phrase 'get down to' is the idiom that precedes this rhyming term for fundamentals

explanation.surface: Fundamentals that one must finally tackle.
explanation.definitionFit: The essential practical facts of a matter, which people speak of getting down to.
